judge_assessment.explanation: Every judge claim is supported. Problem 10 is genuinely typed "manual" with a desc telling the reviewer to read the reasoning, the build exits 2 with '9 passed - 0 failed - 1 manual', and the key does accept the 'fewer longer blocks cover the same straw' argument — it even prints the specific answer NOT to give full credit for ('9 is bigger than 5, so paper clips are longer'). The 'repeated data displays reduce page flipping' finding is literally true: \datapanel is emitted at the top of all three pages. I recomputed everything else from the two displays (Mia 5, Leo 3, Ana 6, Sam 4; crayon 4, marker 6, pencil 7, straw 9): Ana 6; pencil 7 > crayon 4; max Ana; 6-3=3; 9-6=3; total 18; min Leo; ascending 4, 6, 9; Leo+Sam 7 versus Ana+Mia 11 giving '<'. All ten agree with the key. My one qualification is that the answer key's Quick Answers bank prints '2. -' and '9. -' for the two relation comparisons — the same renderer bug as curr-001 — so the at-a-glance column omits two of the nine machine-verified answers. That does not change the ACCEPT.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10 is the model for how the machine/manual boundary should be drawn in this suite: the JSON entry is manual with a desc naming what to look for, the key gives a model sentence, a full-credit rubric ('a drawing showing 5 long blocks and 9 short clips under the same straw earns the same credit') AND a named not-full-credit answer, and final_response.md reports the exit-2 outcome as the correct result rather than as a defect to hide.

\datapanel reprints both the Sticker Chart and the Measuring Strip at the top of every page, so a child answering problem 9 on page 3 never has to flip back for the data — and because the panel is defined once as a macro, the two displays cannot drift between pages.

The interleave is real from problem 1 rather than after a blocked warm-up: read-picture-graph (1, 3, 6), measure-with-units (2, 5, 8, 10) and compare-from-data (4, 7, 9) alternate, and problems 4 and 5 deliberately apply the same 'how many more' move to a graph and to a length so method choice is forced.

Problem 9 is a proper synthesis challenge for the band: Mia's claim is FALSE (7 versus 11), so the student cannot answer by trusting the sentence, and the key warns the grader about the child who compares Sam with Mia instead of the two totals.

root_causes.description: scripts/render_quick_answers.py resolves a string 'expected' by sympify+latex and falls back to a TeX em-dash when sympify raises. A bare relation symbol is not a sympifiable expression, so every compare problem whose order is 'relation' is silently banked as '---' — the marker the module documents as 'manual-only / see solution'. The verified answer exists and is correct; the grader's quick-reference column simply refuses to print it.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '1. 6  2. -  3. Ana  4. 3  5. 3  6. 18  7. Leo  8. 4, 6, 9  9. -  10. -'. Entry 10 is legitimately '-' (manual), but 2 and 9 are verified relations.
verify.json id 2 is compare(['7','4'], relation) -> '>' and id 9 is compare(['3 + 4','5 + 6'], relation) -> '<'; gate_log.txt records both as PASS.
The asc-ordered id 8 renders fine ('4, 6, 9') because its expected is a list, which isolates the fault to the relation branch of _fmt().

improvements.title: Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash instead of the verified relation symbol
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle relation strings in _fmt() BEFORE the sympify attempt: map '<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!=' (and the unicode forms) to '$<$', '$>$', '$=$', '$\le$', '$\ge$', '$\ne$'. sympy.sympify('<') raises SympifyError, so today every compare entry with "order": "relation" drops into the '---' fallback that exists for genuinely unrenderable values. Keep '---' for manual-only ids and for real sympify failures, so the fallback still means 'see the worked solution'.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that renders a verify JSON of [{'id':1,'type':'compare','values':['3','7'],'order':'relation','expected':'<'}, {'id':2,'type':'compare','values':['9','4'],'order':'relation','expected':'>'}, {'id':3,'type':'manual','desc':'open'}] and asserts the bank lines are '$<$', '$>$' and '---' respectively. Today entries 1 and 2 both render '---', so the assertion fails; after the relation mapping it passes, and the manual id still prints '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores problems 2 and 9 to the grading column while leaving problem 10's em-dash correctly in place as the manual marker — which is also why the fix must keep '---' for manual ids rather than removing the fallback.
improvements.risk: Low. Bank entries stay plain text (no \ans/\boxed), so check_answer_key.py's strict per-problem boxed-answer binding is untouched, and column_count() only sees a 3-char string. The only judgement call is math-mode wrapping of '='; both '=' and '$=$' set correctly inside the multicols block.

case_summary: The strongest case in my batch. Ten interleaved measurement and picture-graph questions, all independently recomputed and correct, both data displays reprinted on every page, and — most importantly — an honest machine/manual split: the one open-reasoning item is typed manual with a real rubric and the build exits 2 rather than claiming a verification it cannot make. This is the pattern the flag-open-response-as-manual finding wants everywhere. The only defect is the shared Quick Answers renderer bug, which prints em-dashes for the two relation comparisons.
